The RF Demo Shop answers on a JSON API as well as a web page. Testing the API
directly is fast and checks the **contract** at the seam — no browser needed.

The **RequestsLibrary** provides the HTTP keywords. `GET    <url>` fetches a
resource and returns a response you can assert on.

## Task 1 — Start the RF Demo Shop and keep it running

Start the shop in a terminal and leave it running:

```bash
uv run python demo_app/serve.py
```

Its API is at `http://localhost:7273`.

**Check:** the API answers on its port.

## Task 2 — GET the product catalog and check the count

**Goal:** create `checks/get.robot` that GETs the product catalog, asserts a
`200`, and checks how many products come back.

Here is the same GET-then-assert shape against a different endpoint. Adapt it to
the catalog. (`../resources/api.resource` gives you `${API_URL}`.)

<!-- example -->
```robotframework
*** Settings ***
Library     RequestsLibrary
Resource    ../resources/api.resource

*** Test Cases ***
One Product Responds
    ${resp}=    GET    ${API_URL}/api/products/travel-mug
    Status Should Be    200    ${resp}
    Should Be Equal    ${resp.json()}[slug]    travel-mug
```
<!-- /example -->

**Check:** the GET returns 200 and four products.

<!-- hint -->
The catalog lives at `${API_URL}/api/products` — GET it, then
`Status Should Be    200    ${resp}`.
<!-- /hint -->
<!-- hint -->
The body is a JSON list, so assert its size with
`Length Should Be    ${resp.json()}    4`.
<!-- /hint -->
<!-- solution -->
```robotframework
*** Settings ***
Library     RequestsLibrary
Resource    ../resources/api.resource

*** Test Cases ***
Catalog Lists Products
    ${resp}=    GET    ${API_URL}/api/products
    Status Should Be    200    ${resp}
    Length Should Be    ${resp.json()}    4
```
<!-- /solution -->

**Check:** the GET returns 200 and four products.
